target.title: fix(codex): keep app-server requests aligned with pinned protocol
target.body:
Related: #91878

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the Codex protocol drift check could pass even when OpenClaw's maintained app-server request types no longer matched the pinned Codex wire contract. It could also validate against an unrelated Codex source checkout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The protocol generator now requires the sibling Codex workspace version to exactly match the pinned `@openai/codex` version and compiles a directional compatibility probe against the generated TypeScript types. Maintained request types are tightened to the Codex 0.142.5 contract, while normalized thread and turn response bodies remain owned by the checked-in JSON schemas and projectors. The granular approval helper also emits every field required by the pinned contract.

This is a current-source replay of the valuable portion of #91878. Thanks @vincentkoc for the original investigation and implementation.

## User Impact

Codex app-server requests stay aligned with the exact bundled Codex version, and maintainers get an actionable pre-release failure when either the source checkout or a maintained request shape drifts. No new user configuration is introduced.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_CODEX_REPO=/tmp/openclaw-codex-rust-v0.142.5 pnpm codex-app-server:protocol:check` — passed against the exact `rust-v0.142.5` source; 654 generated TypeScript files checked.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/codex-app-server-protocol-source.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/config.test.ts` — 130 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/codex/tsconfig.json --pretty false` — passed.
- Scoped `pnpm check:changed` — passed on Testbox `tbx_01kwyf97cv8pc5z6xptp8qf8by` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28873550733)).
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on all six changed files — passed.
- Fresh GPT-5.5 autoreview — no accepted or actionable findings.
